A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Graph Concept Bottleneck Models by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–L support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, concept prediction, intervention, ablation, and robustness experiments, including large-scale results in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds a CUB comparison separating message passing from contrastive losses, among other additional results.

M1.justification: The graph parameterization, three-layer message passing, objectives in Equations 1–4, and Lazy Intervention procedure remain unchanged. The new explanation that adjacency matrices receive task-loss and regularizer gradients clarifies the existing formulation rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight datasets, including Places365 and ImageNet in Appendix G, with the same classification, concept prediction, intervention, and corruption scenarios. Adding CIFAR-10 to an ablation table extends analysis within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 newly reports a direct image-feature linear classifier in Section 3.4 and evaluates contrastive-loss-augmented PCBM controls in Figure 4. The named SOTA comparator set in Figure 2 remains unchanged; the newly cited CBM approaches are not added to that comparison.

E3.justification: The new Figure 4 crosses PCBM versus Graph-PCBM with neither, either, or both contrastive losses, adding controls to distinguish their contributions. Existing splits, encoders, training configurations, and intervention procedures in Section 4.1 and Appendices A–D remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 adds the graph-versus-contrastive-loss ablation and extends the loss ablation to CIFAR-10. The existing robustness, graph sparsity, pruning, backbone, and intervention analyses are retained. The additional appendix graph zoom redisplays existing structure.

E5.justification: v2 adds uncertainty values to previously mean-only Tables 2 and 3 and error bars to Figure 2. Previously stated ten-run and four-run counts are retained; the PDFs do not establish an increase in runs or introduce significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises CUB PCBM from 73.84% to 74.69% and Graph-PCBM from 77.14% to 77.95%; Table 4 also updates Graph-PCBM. Table 3 reverses the single-loss score assignments for Flower102 and CIFAR-100 and adds CIFAR-10 results. Figure 4 adds control results, and Section 3.4 reports 81.19% for direct feature classification. These are reported revisions and additions, without evidence explaining reruns.

T1.justification: The mathematical graph formulation, message-passing and loss equations, and Appendix D intervention definitions are retained. Added dimensional explanations and an informal parameter-count argument introduce no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: learnable concept graphs improve prediction and intervention, expose concept relationships, and integrate across supervised and label-free CBMs. The rewritten abstract does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds an information-loss explanation for concept bottlenecks and interprets Figure 4 as showing that message passing drives the gains more than contrastive learning alone. It also argues against model capacity as the explanation and revises the motivation for structural self-supervision. The stated hierarchy limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an implementation-repository link in the abstract and explicitly documents joint optimization of adjacency matrices through cross-entropy and regularizers. The hardware, batch sizes, training times, and hyperparameter tables in Appendix B are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds Editable CBMs, DCBM, and Causally Reliable CBMs, expands discussion of the already cited Stochastic CBM, and contrasts task-adaptive graph learning with causal constraints. Maron and Bronstein references support the existing permutation-invariance discussion. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, related work and the method overview are expanded, and explanatory paragraphs are added around optimization and ablations. Citations switch to author–year style. The main section sequence and Appendices A–L retain their organization.

P2.justification: v2 adopts document-wide TMLR typography, author layout, headers, and revised figure placement. Tables gain highlighting, Table 3 is reorganized, and Figure 2 gains percentage axes and error bars. A new ablation figure and enlarged appendix graph view are added; the full-graph display drops its accompanying concept-pair list.

improvement.justification: The added graph-versus-loss controls, broader uncertainty reporting, and implementation link modestly strengthen evidential support and reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by unreconciled CUB values: Tables 1 and 4 report 77.95%, while Section 4.6 retains 77.14%. The new claim excluding model capacity also lacks a matched-capacity control. The revision improves documentation and analysis without resolving all evidential weaknesses.
